statement: The arithmetic tier beneath J-depth-one-main-term, machine-checked. (a) dual_phase: for the phase F(M) = alpha M^(3/2), at the stationary point M_nu = s^2 with s = 2 nu / (3 alpha) (stationary_point) the Legendre value alpha s^3 - nu s^2 equals -4 nu^3 / (27 alpha^2), a cubic whose coefficient is rational whenever alpha is; at alpha = 1/2 it is -16 nu^3 / 27 (dual_phase_half), so the dual modulus is 27. dual_phase_rpow states the same with the half-power written as a real power, alpha M^(3/2) - nu M at M = (2 nu/(3 alpha))^2, via rpow_three_halves_of_sq. This is where the exponent 3/2 enters: its dual exponent is the integer 3. (b) completeCubicSum_eq_nine: sum over r < 27 of e(-16 r^3 / 27) = 9 exactly, with e(theta) = exp(2 pi i theta). The proof is structural, not a numerical evaluation: every term is zeta^(11 r^3 mod 27) for zeta = e(1/27) (dual_term, zeta27_pow_mod), nine residues cube to 0, and the eighteen others fall into two triples in arithmetic progression of common difference 9, each killed by 1 + zeta^9 + zeta^18 = 0 (zeta27_nine_sum, since zeta^9 is a primitive cube root of unity). (c) depthOneConstant_eq_sqrt_six_div_nine: the constant (4 sqrt8 / 27)(3/4)^(3/2) that the note prints and measures to four digits is exactly sqrt6 / 9 = 0.2721655..., a closed form the note does not record; depthOneConstant_eq_printed ties the definition to the printed half-power form via rpow_three_halves. (d) sum_affine_reindex with two_isUnit: a complete sum over ZMod n is unchanged by x -> u x + c for a unit u, and 2 is a unit modulo 27 k^2 for every odd k, which is the step the note calls '2 nu + 1 runs over a complete residue system' and is the mechanism that cancels the two X^(3/4) terms over odd M. The character convention matches CircleMethod.e on prove2.me, so the statements port in both directions. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. The asymptotic itself (B-process remainders, Erdos-Turan) is not asserted here and stays with J-depth-one-main-term.

The depth-one parity sum has a main term, and the Juggler odd branch cancels it in every harmonic. The van der Corput B-process dualises F(M) = alpha M^(3/2) to -4 nu^3/(27 alpha^2), a cubic with rational coefficient, so the dual sum is a complete cubic Gauss sum on every period; at alpha = 1/2 the modulus is 27, the sum is 9, and |sum_{M<=X} e(M^(3/2)/2)| = (4 sqrt8/27)(3/4)^(3/2) X^(3/4)(1+o(1)) = 0.27217 X^(3/4), measured 0.2701, 0.2707, 0.2721, 0.2719 at 1e5, 1e6, 1e7, 5e7. The parity of floor(M^(3/2)) is biased toward even by 0.425 X^(3/4), entirely on even M. For every odd harmonic k the parity twist moves the stationary points to half-integers and, 2 being invertible mod 27k^2, the twisted and untwisted complete sums coincide (C_k = 9k for 3 not dividing k, C_9 = 0), so all X^(3/4) terms cancel on odd M; with the B-process remainders and Erdos-Turan at H = X^(1/2) this gives #{n <= X odd : floor(n^(3/2)) odd} = X/4 + O(X^(1/2+eps)) (HUMAN PROOF sketch), against the O(X^(3/4)) of the second-derivative test that is attained over even n. Measured, the odd-restricted harmonic sums are 1.3-3.4 X^(1/4) for k = 1,3,5,7 and the parity imbalance over odd n is 30, 146, 210, 16 at 1e5-5e7. Tower levels 2-4 over odd starts to 1e7 carry only sqrt-order imbalance. The arithmetic tier of this row is now machine-checked in formal/Problems/Juggler/DepthOneMainTerm.lean (row J-depth-one-arithmetic-layer): the rational-cubic dual, the complete cubic sum 9, the affine invariance behind the odd-start cancellation, and the constant in the exact closed form sqrt6/9. What stays HUMAN PROOF is the analytic tier: the B-process remainders and the Erdos-Turan step, hence the asymptotic and the X/4 + O(X^(1/2+eps)) count. Exact and depth-one only. CLOSE. Not a halt theorem.
